div.head: III Atr 15
div.ab: And se þe reafað man leohtan dǽge, ⁊ he hit kyþe to þrim túnan, þæt he ne beo nanes fryðes weorðe.
[15] Et qui robauerit hominem in luce diei, et in tribus uillis indicabit, non habeatur simile ac si concelasset.
And se þe reafað man leohtan dǽge ⁊ he hit kyþe to þrim túnan, þæt he ne beo nanes fryðes weorðe.
Und wer einen Menschen am lichten Tage beraubt, und [wenn] der es in drei Ortschaften kund macht: dass jener keines Friedenschutzes theilhaftig sei.
And whoever robs a person in broad daylight, and [if] the latter makes it known in three villages: that the robber is not entitled to any protection.
And if a man robs another in daylight, and the latter makes the deed known in three villages, he shall not be entitled to protection of any kind.
And he who robs a man in daylight, and the latter announces it in three villages, is to be entitled to no asylum.
div.note: Quadr.'s version (‘non habeatur simile ac si concelasset’ = let it not be treated as if he had concealed it) differs.

Die Verkennung des Subjektwechsels verführt entweder Q dazu, an einen Räuber zu denken, der wegen Kundmachung seines Tuns anders [d. i. milder] zu behandeln sei als der heimliche (s. d. Gl 1d. 2) Verbrecher, vermutlich an einen sich berechtigt glaubenden Rächer. Oder aber die Wörter [pacis dignus] sind von Q nur unabsichtlich ausgelassen; dann gilt die Deutung in Gl Kundmachung 4

Failure to recognize the change of subject either leads Q to think of a robber who, because he made his deed known, is to be treated differently [i.e. more leniently] than the secret (see that word in Gl 1d. 2) criminal, presumably of an avenger who believes himself to be in the right. Or else the words [pacis dignus] have merely been omitted by Q unintentionally; in that case the interpretation in Gl Kundmachung 4 holds
Vgl. Gl Dorf 7a. e. f. Price denkt als Zentrum Tatort oder Heimat des Beraubten; mir scheint ersterer gemeint
Cf. Gl Dorf 7a. e. f. Price takes the centre to be the scene of the crime or the home of the man robbed; I think the former is meant
